what: Warner Music Group is one of the three major record companies. It signs and distributes recorded music and, through Warner Chappell, owns the rights to songs themselves, earning from every stream, radio play and licensed use.
customers: Streaming services such as Spotify and Apple Music, broadcasters, advertisers, film and game producers, and concert promoters.
money: streaming, physical sales and artist services
songwriting royalties from performance, mechanical and sync rights
moat: Ownership of a catalogue of recordings and songs that must be licensed by anyone who wants to play them, with rights that last for decades.
risks: Streaming subscriber growth in developed markets has slowed
Negotiating power is concentrated in a few streaming platforms
Artificial intelligence generated music is an unresolved threat to catalogue value
opportunities: Streaming price increases flow through to it with almost no added cost
Emerging market streaming adoption is still in early stages
watch: Streaming revenue growth and subscription price increases at the major platforms.
